title: How Can You Spot Fake News? Talk to Others!
paragraphs: Whether it's in videos or in written articles, it feels like it's getting harder and harder to spot fake news these days.
But one of the simplest things we can do to spot fake news is talk to other people!
Researchers from Italy did a study with 111 university students. The participants were given two fake news stories and two real ones, and were asked to rate how likely each story was to be true.
Then, for two of the stories, the participants had to write out their reasoning for their "truth" rating, then rated it again.

For the other two stories, the participants were put into groups of three, and each participant was given time to talk about their reasoning for their "truth" rating. After each discussion, they rated the story again.
Half the participants did their two written answers first, and half did the two discussions first.
It was found that, after they stopped to think about their reasoning alone, there was no real difference in how accurately people rated the truth of the stories.
However, after group discussion about a fake news story, participants were better able to identify it as fake.
And participants who discussed one of the fake stories in a group first were better able to spot the other fake story on their own afterward.
When participants were grouped with people who had been better at spotting the two fake stories at the beginning of the experiment, 73% became more accurate after the group discussion.
By comparison, only 36% became less accurate after being grouped with people who were bad at spotting fake news — meaning most people weren't influenced by incorrect reasoning.
So, the next time you read a news story you're not too sure about, it might help to talk to a friend!
